nodes.title: Privatelink: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Privatelink. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: An application team exposes a Kubernetes service via an internal NLB in VPC-A. C?
flashcards.back: AWS PrivateLink uses a producer (VPC Endpoint Service backed by an NLB) and consumer (Interface Endpoint) model, ideal for cross-account service exposure without requiring VPC-level connectivity. This avoids CIDR-overlap concerns, does not require peering or TGW attachments, and only the specific service is exposed. Peering and TGW create network-level connectivity, which is more than what is needed. Route 53 alone does not provide private connectivity.

flashcards.front: A company wants to use Interface VPC Endpoints (PrivateLink) to access Amazon S3?
flashcards.back: AWS offers both S3 Gateway Endpoints (free, route-table based, in-VPC only) and S3 Interface Endpoints (PrivateLink, charged per hour + data processed, support access from on-premises and cross-VPC/account). Many architectures use both. Interface Endpoints for S3 are globally available, not GovCloud-only. and/or Gateway Endpoints for in-VPC access at no additional charge

flashcards.front: A company wants to enforce that all VPC endpoints created in member accounts mus?
flashcards.back: Organization-wide enforcement of VPC endpoint policies is achieved by combining SCPs (deny creation of non-compliant endpoints), Config rules (detect non-compliant endpoints), and automated remediation (SSM / Lambda). AWS Firewall Manager focuses on SG/WAF/NFW/DNS Firewall policies, not generic endpoint policies. RAM is sharing, not policy enforcement. Shield is DDoS-focused.

flashcards.front: A company has a private ALB in a VPC and wants to expose it to customers over Pr?
flashcards.back: VPC Endpoint Services (PrivateLink provider side) can be backed by NLBs or GWLBs. To expose an ALB via PrivateLink, you create an NLB with ALB-type target (supported since 2021), then create the VPC Endpoint Service on that NLB. Consumers use Interface Endpoints. You cannot create an endpoint service directly from an ALB. API Gateway is unrelated.

pairs.stem: A company wants to use Interface VPC Endpoints (PrivateLink) to access Amazon S3 from within a VPC without going through the public internet. Which statement is accurate?
pairs.option: You can use S3 Interface Endpoints (PrivateLink) for cross-VPC or on-premises access.

pairs.stem: An application team exposes a Kubernetes service via an internal NLB in VPC-A. Consumers in VPC-B (different AWS account, same Region) must access this service privately without VPC peering or Transit Gateway attachments. Which solution is appropriate?
pairs.option: Create a VPC Endpoint Service (PrivateLink) on VPC-A's NLB and create an Interface Endpoint in VPC-B pointing to that service

pairs.stem: A company has a VPC endpoint (Interface) for an AWS service and wants to restrict which IAM principals can use it. Which mechanism enforces this at the endpoint level?
pairs.option: AWS RAM share permissions on the endpoint

pairs.stem: A company has a private ALB in a VPC and wants to expose it to customers over PrivateLink (Interface Endpoints). What must the company configure?
pairs.option: Create a VPC Endpoint Service directly from the ALB

pairs.stem: A company wants to enforce that all VPC endpoints created in member accounts must use an endpoint policy restricting access to specific S3 buckets. Which AWS service can enforce this at scale across accounts?
pairs.option: AWS Shield Advanced with endpoint enforcement

pairs.stem: A company has an EC2 instance in a private subnet without internet access. It must reach an Amazon Kinesis stream privately. What is the simplest solution?
pairs.option: Create an Interface VPC Endpoint (PrivateLink) for Kinesis in the VPC

nodes.title: Cloudfront: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Cloudfront. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: A media streaming company uses CloudFront with an S3 origin serving premium cont?
flashcards.back: Origin Access Control (OAC) is the modern replacement for OAI, supporting SigV4 and SSE-KMS. CloudFront signed URLs are the standard short-lived token mechanism. CloudFront geo restriction (or WAF geo match rule) blocks countries. Shield Advanced is for DDoS, not geo-blocking. S3 pre-signed URLs would expose the bucket directly. use CloudFront signed URLs for short-lived tokens, and apply CloudFront geo restriction (or AWS WAF geo match rule) to block restricted countries

flashcards.front: A company has an ALB behind CloudFront and needs to ensure CloudFront viewers ca?
flashcards.back: The recommended patterns are either (1) using the AWS Managed Prefix List for CloudFront (com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing) in the ALB security group, or (2) using a custom header on CloudFront and a WAF rule on the ALB validating it. Both prevent direct access. Lambda maintaining IP lists is outdated. GWLB is not suitable. A private ALB with no NAT would not be reachable from CloudFront either.

flashcards.front: A company uses CloudFront in front of multiple origins and wants to selectively ?
flashcards.back: CloudFront Functions run at all 600+ edge locations, have sub-millisecond startup, cost fraction vs Lambda@Edge, and are designed for lightweight header manipulation, URL rewrites, and simple auth checks. Lambda@Edge works but has higher latency, cost, and runs only at regional edge caches. WAF response headers are for WAF actions, not general manipulation. Origin Shield is a regional cache layer, not transformation.

flashcards.front: A company has a CloudFront distribution serving content from multiple origins gl?
flashcards.back: CloudFront Origin Shield is an additional centralized cache layer that consolidates requests from all edge locations, dramatically reducing origin load and improving cache hit ratios. Higher TTLs help but cannot always be used. CloudFront Functions and Lambda@Edge are for transformations, not cache consolidation.

pairs.stem: A company has a CloudFront distribution serving content from multiple origins globally. They notice that requests during traffic spikes sometimes bypass the regional cache and hit the origin directly, increasing origin load. Which feature reduces origin load during spikes?
pairs.option: Enable CloudFront Origin Shield in a Region close to the origin to provide an additional centralized cache layer and reduce origin requests

pairs.stem: A company has an ALB behind CloudFront and needs to ensure CloudFront viewers cannot bypass CloudFront and hit the ALB directly. Which method provides this enforcement with the least maintenance overhead?
pairs.option: Place the ALB in a private subnet without a NAT Gateway so only CloudFront can reach it

pairs.stem: A company wants to monitor ISP-level performance issues affecting their internet-facing applications worldwide and automatically correlate them with their AWS resources. Which AWS service provides this capability?

A company uses CloudFront in front of multiple origins and wants to selectively modify viewer request headers (to add a geolocation header) before they reach the origin. Requirements: extremely low-latency, simple logic, no package dependencies. Which feature fits best?
pairs.option: CloudFront Functions running at edge locations for lightweight JavaScript manipulations on viewer-request and viewer-response events

pairs.stem: A media streaming company uses CloudFront with an S3 origin serving premium content. Requirements: (1) block direct access to the S3 bucket so that content is only accessible via CloudFront, (2) support signed URLs with short-lived tokens, (3) block countries under trade restrictions. Which combination implements all requirements?
pairs.option: Configure Origin Access Control (OAC) with SigV4.

pairs.stem: A company uses AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to issue public TLS certificates for ALBs and CloudFront. They want to automatically rotate certificates without manual intervention. Which statement is accurate?
pairs.option: ACM public certificates must be rotated manually every 13 months

nodes.title: Mixed Topics: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Mixed Topics. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: A financial services company needs a hybrid DNS architecture where on-premises D?
flashcards.back: Route 53 Resolver endpoints solve hybrid DNS. Inbound endpoints receive DNS queries from on-premises (for AWS private zones), while outbound endpoints forward DNS queries from AWS to on-premises resolvers using forwarding rules tied to domain names. This is the AWS-recommended hybrid DNS pattern. DHCP Option Sets with custom DNS servers work but require you to manage BIND yourself. Public hosted zones are not appropriate for internal names.

flashcards.front: A company uses Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall to block requests to known malicio?
flashcards.back: Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall supports AWS Managed Domain Lists such as malware and botnet C&C lists that are continuously updated. You associate them into a rule group with BLOCK action and associate the rule group with VPCs. GuardDuty detects but does not directly block DNS. Manual lists require ongoing maintenance. AWSManagedDomainsBotnetCommandandControl) to a DNS Firewall rule group with a BLOCK action, then associate the rule group with the VPC

flashcards.front: A regulated customer requires all DNS traffic within their VPCs to go through th?
flashcards.back: A forwarding rule with domain name '.' (root) configured on an outbound endpoint forwards all DNS queries to on-premises targets. The rule must be associated with the relevant VPCs. Disabling VPC DNS would break internal AWS resolution. Inbound endpoints are for on-prem to AWS queries. Private hosted zones do not provide forwarding.

flashcards.front: A global company uses Route 53 with latency-based routing and health checks for ?
flashcards.back: Latency-based routing returns the record with the lowest latency among healthy records. If Singapore users get routed to eu-west-1, the ap-southeast-1 record is likely unhealthy (failing health check), missing, or misconfigured. Verify health check status and that the record is properly tagged with Region=ap-southeast-1. Latency routing is not region-restricted. the health check is failing, or the record is not associated with the correct region/latency base; verify the health check status and record configuration

pairs.stem: A global company uses Route 53 with latency-based routing and health checks for an application deployed in us-east-1, eu-west-1, and ap-southeast-1. Users in Singapore report being routed to eu-west-1 even though ap-southeast-1 is healthy. What is the most likely cause?
pairs.option: The ap-southeast-1 DNS record is missing.

pairs.stem: A company needs to share a Transit Gateway across 25 AWS accounts in an AWS Organization to attach VPCs from each account. Which service enables this sharing model?
pairs.option: Create a cross-account IAM role in the TGW owner account that grants ec2:AttachTransitGateway

pairs.stem: An organization requires that all outbound internet traffic from EKS pods in a VPC originate from specific static IPs so that SaaS vendors can allowlist them. Which architecture accomplishes this?
pairs.option: Deploy a Network Load Balancer in front of the outbound traffic

pairs.stem: A financial services company needs a hybrid DNS architecture where on-premises DNS servers can resolve records in AWS Route 53 private hosted zones, and AWS resources can resolve internal company domains hosted on-premises. What is the correct configuration?
pairs.option: Create Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoints for on-premises queries into AWS and outbound endpoints with forwarding rules for AWS queries to on-premises

pairs.stem: A company uses Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall to block requests to known malicious domains. They want high-confidence AWS-managed blocklists that are continuously updated. Which configuration should be used?
pairs.option: Associate the AWS Managed Domain Lists (AWSManagedDomainsMalwareDomainList.

pairs.stem: A customer has a VPC with CIDR 10.0.0.0/16 and needs to add more IP space without changing existing subnets. They also want to use the new space for EKS pods. Which approach is correct?
pairs.option: Add a /22 CIDR block from the 172.16.0.0/12 range, which is the only supported range for EKS
